page.layout: One text column in the centre. Two marginal notes in the left margin, the first beside the opening lines of the column and the second beside its middle. No notes on the right, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: Menstruæ olim In marg. Cephafi [?] ad eun. locum. contactu contraxisse tradunt (referentibus Zamach. in Comm. ad caput secundum Alc. Ahmede Ebn Yusef &c.) vel ut alii, ab ipso Mohammedis ore acceptâ mutati coloris ratione, cùm è Paradiso defcendiffet اشد بياضا من اللبن candore plus quàm lacteo, سودته خطايا بني آدم nigredinem illi conciliâsse hominum peccata: quam tamen adhuc في راسه ... ون ساد caput, vel exteriorem tantùm ejus partem pervasisse, reliquis partibus albedinem pristinam retinentibus, palam factum quo tempore à Karmatiü loco suo motus est, testatur Ahmed Ebn Yusef; adeo ut ab osculantium anhelitu ac contactu foedatum, ut alibi me legisse, vel saltem à Mohammedanis accepisse memini, credibile sit. Fuisse eum ex illis qui olim Idololatricè culti facilè crediderim. Quâ cum hunc superstitione venerentur Mohammedis sectatores, cùm in religionis ab ipso traditæ fundamenta inquirendum infra fuerit, videbimus. Quod autem à Damasceno, & Eutbymio asseritur, si quis accuratiùs infpectet videri in eo figuram capitis scal-pro expressam, quod Venerù esse volunt, ex Arabum scriptis puto probari non posse. Alius illis lapis est sacer, cui insculptam, vel potiùs impressam, tradunt figuram, sed tantùm à figura capitis quantum caput à pedibus distantem; nisi oculi superstitione lippi caput à pedibus distinguere nesciant. Lapis sc. in quo vestigia pedum Abrahami impressa; cùm vel illi inter ædificandum Caabam insisteret, ut innuit Abulfeda; vel dum ipsi caput, Ismaelis, quem visum venerat, uxor (ut Ahmed Ebn Yusef, & Safioddinus) lavaret. Unde & illi nomen مقام ابراهيم Makam Abrahim. Locus (scil.) Abrahami, vel, quo fletit Abrahamus. In vit. Ismael habet etiam Safiod.

page.notes: Marginal notes: the first is written as "Ceo / fhafi" in the scan and is read as "Cephafi" with a doubt; the second is in the left margin beside "Ismaelis". Arabic words are copied from the scan; the phrase after "quam tamen adhuc" is not legible beyond the first word and its last letters are doubtful. The Arabic name "Makam Abrahim" is read with a doubt on the final letters. The Arabic in the text was set with the Latin and printed in the same line, so its exact placement may differ. Some Latin lines are broken at the line end with a printed hyphen (scal-pro).
